title: Smooth fibre branches give a Zariski strict pair chart
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed] and $V\subseteq K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, meaning that for $z\in K^\times$ either $z$ or $z^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Suppose the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-curve here is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with pure one-dimensional fibres [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], without any separatedness or properness assumption. A curve is semistable if every nonsmooth point of every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $(X,D)$ be a semistable multipointed $S$-curve with smooth generic curve. Here $X$ is a semistable $S$-curve and $D\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], with $D\to S$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], finitely presented and of pure relative dimension zero, and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus of $X\to S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; $D$ may be empty. For every $s\in S$, give the irreducible components of $X_s$ their reduced induced closed-subscheme structures [def-weil-irreducible-components, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Assume that every such component of every fibre is smooth over $\kappa(s)$ at all its points. Then for every $x\in X$, with $s=x|_S$, there are affine Zariski open neighbourhoods $x\in U\subseteq X$ and $s\in S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$, with $U\to S$ factoring through $S_0$, and an etale morphism of pairs over $S_0$ from $(U,D\cap U)$ to one of
$$(\operatorname{Spec}A[z],\{z=0\}),\qquad (\operatorname{Spec}A[u,v]/(uv-c),\varnothing),\quad c\in A.$$
An etale morphism of pairs means compatible etale maps of curves and of markings. At a marked point one can choose the first chart with $D\cap U$ the inverse image of $z=0$; at a nonsmooth point one can choose the second chart. At a smooth unmarked point the first chart is allowed with empty marking on its source. Polynomial rings have their ordinary meaning [def-weil-polynomial-ring].

source.place: §4.3, definition of strict semistable pairs and the smooth-component observation, printed p. 27; Remark 4.5.2, printed p. 33. Agent-reconstructed relative all-fibres smooth-branch criterion over the finite-height separably closed valuation base; Stacks Tag 0CBY, curves.tex, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family supplies only etale neighbourhoods, not this Zariski conclusion. Local archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: First treat the relative smooth locus. At a marked $x$, shrink into that locus and apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] to the closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ over $S$. Since the relative dimensions are $0$ and $1$, its integers are $a=0,b=1$. The resulting etale map to $\mathbf A^1_S$ has $D\cap U$ exactly the inverse image of $0$ and restricts to an etale marking map. At a smooth unmarked point remove the closed subset $D$ and apply [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form]; the relative dimension is $1$, so its affine space is $\mathbf A^1$. Its empty marking maps etale to the zero section. Restrict both charts to affine neighbourhoods of $x$ and $s$.

source.place: Smooth and marked cases; more-morphisms.tex, lemma-etale-local-structure (adapted coordinates), and morphisms.tex, local normal form of a smooth morphism.

proof.text: Now let $x$ be nonsmooth. Remove $D$ and take an affine open around $x$. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model] to get a pointed etale nodal chart $Y\to X$ over an etale base neighbourhood $T\to S$. Refine $T$ to an affine neighbourhood of the image of the chosen point of $Y$. The valuation ring is normal: if $z\notin V$, then $z^{-1}\in\mathfrak m_V$, and a monic integral equation for $z$, divided by its top power, would put $1$ in $\mathfrak m_V$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-finite-etale-section] with its ambient affine normal integral scheme equal to $S$ and its closed subscheme equal to $S$ itself. The chosen component of $T$ is an open subscheme $S_0$ of $S$. Restricting to it replaces the base by a Zariski open, not the source chart by an open. Thus we have etale maps $p:Y\to X$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A[u_0,v_0]/(u_0v_0-c)$ for $c\in A$, and a chosen point over $x$ at $u_0=v_0=0$. The chosen point maps to $u_0=v_0=0$: the standard model is smooth off that locus by its Jacobian, and smoothness at a point is preserved and reflected by an etale source neighbourhood. For reflection restrict its smooth open to its open image and use [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent]. Here and below, etale composition and base change are the scheme-source case of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] supply preservation of smoothness. The openness used is [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open].

source.place: Initial etale neighbourhood from lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-closed-of-affine-normal-scheme-with-alg-closed-function-field removes the base neighbourhood.

proof.text: Here $A$ is again a valuation subring of $K$ of finite height. Its generic fibre is the original smooth generic curve. Therefore $c\ne0$: if $c=0$, the generic node $u_0=v_0=0$ is a generalization of the chosen standard-model node. The open image of the etale map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A[u_0,v_0]/(u_0v_0)$ would contain it, producing a nonsmooth generic point of $Y$, contrary to smoothness of $X_K$ and etaleness of $p_K$. In particular $u_0$ and $v_0$ are nonzerodivisors on $Y$, since their product is the nonzero base element $c$ and $Y$ is flat over $A$. They are invertible on $Y_K$. Apply [lem-trf-ordered-nodal-branch-overlap] to this chart. Replace $X,Y$ by its affine opens $U,Y_0$; $p_0:Y_0\to U$ is a surjective etale affine morphism and the two pullbacks of each coordinate generate equal ideals at all fibre-generic points of $W=Y_0\times_UY_0$. Openness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]; the etale permanence and smooth-composition statements cited here justify restriction to the generic fibre.

source.place: Nonzero thickness and branch ordering on the existing chart; the source gives no Zariski replacement of the source neighbourhood.

proof.text: The scheme $W$ is affine, flat and finitely presented over $A$; it is etale over $Y_0$. For a geometric fibre, compose its etale maps to the standard nodal model. That model is reduced: when the parameter is nonzero it is a Laurent polynomial ring; when it is zero the ideal $(uv)=(u)\cap(v)$ is radical. Hence [etale-proposition-etale-reduced] makes the geometric fibre of $W$ reduced. Etale composition and base change here use [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Apply [lem-trf-vertical-principal-ideal-fibre-detection] on $W$ to the two pullbacks of $u_0$, and then to the two pullbacks of $v_0$. Its generic-unit hypothesis holds because $u_0v_0=c\ne0$ on the generic fibre; its fibre-generic equalities are exactly those of Step 3. We obtain equality of the two pulled-back ideal sheaves $(u_0)$ on every overlap, and likewise for $(v_0)$. These are equalities as submodules of $\mathcal O_W$, not chosen isomorphisms of abstract line modules, so their canonical identifications automatically satisfy the triple-overlap cocycle.

source.place: Upgrade fibre-generic comparisons to equality of the vertical principal ideals; agent reconstruction using the separately stated finite-height detection lemma.

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] for the affine faithfully flat quasi-compact cover $p_0:Y_0\to U$. Apply its equivalence to the two ideal modules and their inclusions into $\mathcal O_{Y_0}$, with the canonical descent data of Step 4. Full faithfulness descends the inclusions; their kernels vanish because they vanish after a faithfully flat pullback. It gives invertible ideal sheaves $I,J\subset\mathcal O_U$ whose pullbacks are $(u_0),(v_0)$. The product equality $(u_0)(v_0)=(c)$ descends too, hence $IJ=(c)$. Zariski locally around $x$ choose generators $u,v$ of $I,J$. Their product generates $(c)$, so $uv=\varepsilon c$ for a unit $\varepsilon$. Replacing $v$ by $\varepsilon^{-1}v$ gives $uv=c$, hence an actual morphism $h:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A[u,v]/(uv-c)$. On $Y_0$ one has $p_0^*u=\alpha u_0$, $p_0^*v=\alpha^{-1}v_0$ for a unit $\alpha$: cancel the nonzerodivisor $c$ to see that the two rescaling units are inverse.

source.place: Effective descent of quasi-coherent modules and rank-one local freeness; descent.tex, effective fpqc descent. Construction of the Zariski-local generators written out.

proof.text: Check etaleness of $h p_0$ at every point of $Y_0$ above $x$. There both $u_0,v_0$ vanish. Introduce an invertible variable $t$ on $E=Y_0\times\mathbf G_m$ and map $E$ to the nodal model by $(u,v)=(tu_0,t^{-1}v_0)$. The map $E\to(\operatorname{Spec}A[u,v]/(uv-c))\times\mathbf G_m$ is etale: after the invertible change $(u,v,t)\mapsto(t^{-1}u,tv,t)$ it is the base change of the original chart. The graph $t=\alpha$ is $Y_0$ and its composite to the nodal model is $h p_0$. In a square Jacobian presentation for this etale map, eliminate its chart variables and add the equation $F=t-\alpha$. Differentiation over the nodal model gives $du_0=-u_0\,dt/t$ and $dv_0=v_0\,dt/t$. Thus $d\alpha/dt=0$ at these points, and $\partial F/\partial t=1$. The enlarged square Jacobian is invertible. By [lem-exc-etale-jacobian-presentation], the graph is etale over the nodal model near each such point. This is a direct Jacobian calculation, with no assertion that a fibrewise tangent isomorphism alone proves etaleness of a relative morphism.

source.place: Square-Jacobian calculation for inverse unit rescaling of nodal coordinates; algebraic etale presentation criterion.

proof.text: Shrink $Y_0$ to the open where $h p_0$ is etale. Step 6 shows that this open contains every point over $x$, and its image under $p_0$ is an open neighbourhood $U'$ of $x$. The restricted map to $U'$ is a surjective etale cover. Apply [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] to conclude that $h|_{U'}$ is etale. Choose an affine Zariski neighbourhood of $x$ in $U'$. The marking is empty because the original nodal neighbourhood was disjoint from $D$; its map to the empty standard marking is etale. Together with Step 1 this proves every chart and the extra assertions at marked, nonsmooth and smooth unmarked points.

source.place: descent.tex, lemma-etale-etale-local-source: descend the checked etaleness through the source cover, then choose an affine open.
